title: BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit

# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX audit

## Scope and evidence standard

This is an evidence-led audit rather than a feature wish-list. “Pain point” means an explicit warning, workaround, multi-step dependency, or user description found in a source. Where a requested limit could not be verified, it is marked **not verified** rather than inferred. In particular, the public PTSEQUENCER sources I found do not expose a primary manual; the 2047 figure is only community-reported.

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Open/drag audio → place or import markers → snap/offset/zero-cross and preview → save project → export keysounds and BMSE/iBMSC clipboard/list data. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) | 1) Zero-cross reduces clicks but moves markers; iBMSC output can produce missing keysounds or gamemode changes, so README recommends BMSE rounding. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) 2) Large-file loading and non-stereo waveform/offset preview needed fixes. [release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/vb28b1af) [release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/v74831ea) 3) BPM-change support is partial and better grid/clipboard support is still planned. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features) | No numeric slice-count ceiling documented; snap 1/1–1/192, plus arbitrary snap. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) | WAV/keysound export; BMSE clipboard rounds to 192nd; iBMSC clipboard preserves finer resolution; keysound list can be copied/appended to BMS. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts) |
| **Woslicer II** | Drag WAV → set BPM/offset → add markers and choose grid → preview → batch WAV output → clipboard export into BMSE. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | 1) Unsupported/unreadable WAV can crash; re-save with SoundEngine Free/Audacity and check 24/32-bit. [wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer) 2) Leading silence/offset must be aligned manually. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) 3) Export/placement depends on correct starting definition number and clipboard handoff. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | Guide documents default 1/16 grid; Woslicer III guide documents up to 192 divisions/bar. No slice-count ceiling found. [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Batch WAV (“M”), clipboard export, then BMSE paste. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) |
| **Woslicer III** | BMHelper MIDI → DAW render → drag rendered WAV → copy BMHelper cut positions → clipboard import → set BPM → “export all”; or manually click chop points for non-MIDI/automation parts. [guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) | 1) The author calls sound cutting the most troublesome/long step and says manual “ぶつ切り” is for cases BMHelper cannot handle. [guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) 2) Export is file-oriented: WAV plus WOS metadata, then delete unwanted silent tail files/markers. [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) 3) Every key/BGM file should stay under one minute (guide recommends about 50 s); this is a downstream compliance constraint, not a slicer maximum. [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Up to 192 divisions/bar; no numeric slice-count ceiling found. [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | WAV export, WOS save, and clipboard sequence/position export. [guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) |
| **BMHelper / Mid2BMS** | BMHelper: import MIDI → split/reduce/rearrange → render MIDI-derived audio → Woslicer cuts it → paste sequence/definitions into BMSE. Mid2BMS combines MIDI-to-BMS and slicing functions and outputs renamer/definition data. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) [Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/) | 1) BMHelper itself does not slice audio and assumes Woslicer/BMSE. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) 2) MIDI compatibility can fail; documented workaround is routing/re-saving MIDI through another DAW/MIDI editor. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) 3) Mid2BMS documents a renamer-array error workaround (delete first four lines; later marked fixed). [Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/) | No maximum documented in retrieved sources; quantization/chord slicing advertised by Mid2BMS. [Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/) | MIDI, renamer arrays, BMS sequence/definition clipboard; audio export still requires DAW/Woslicer in the documented workflow. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) |
| **BMSE / iBMSC** | Import/define hundreds of WAV/OGG files → paste clipboard timing/sequence data → place/edit notes → save BMS and same-folder assets. [guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) | 1) File ordering and definition start position must match drag order. [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) 2) Locale decimal comma can require post-export find/replace. [guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) 3) Default 192nd snapping can audibly change sound; finer grids may trigger overlap warnings. [checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/) | Traditional BMS guide: 1295 keysounds; BMSE/Base62 note reports 3843, but compatibility is engine/editor dependent. [guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | External WAV/OGG files plus clipboard text/BMS definitions. [guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) |
| **dtinth/sound-slicer** | `.txt` marker description + WAV → sliced WAVs and BMS clipboard; rhythmic or melodic MIDI-to-text mode. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Rhythmic mode makes one slice per event and explicitly does not deduplicate similar sounds (1000 notes → 1000 slices). Melodic mode reduces repeated bassline example from 500 to 10 but requires render → re-import → slice → paste. Neither mode supports BPM changes. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | No numeric maximum; no BPM-change support documented. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Sliced WAVs in a `wav` subfolder plus generated BMS clipboard. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) |
| **FL Studio Fruity Slicer** | Load WAV/REX → auto/beat/marker slice → edit slice properties → play from Piano roll/controller; optionally send to BeatSlicer or save processed sample. [manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm) | MP3 cannot carry slice markers; longer loops are harder to guess accurately; imperfect markers require external editing and reload. [manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm) | No numeric maximum found; supports beat divisions and zero-cross check. [manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm) | Plugin/sample save and BeatSlicer handoff, not BMS clipboard. [manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm) |
| **PTSEQUENCER** | DJMAX internal pattern-authoring tool referenced in community documentation. | Exact public workflow, shortcuts, export, and current limit were not verified from a primary manual. NamuWiki reports older 1023 and DPC 2025 2047 figures; treat as community-reported, not a product contract. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | **Unverified as primary fact:** 1023/2047 reported by NamuWiki. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | Not publicly documented in the retrieved sources. |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline — P0/P1

- **P0 — Timing is split across audio time, BPM grid, and editor grid.** Woslicer requires BPM and offset alignment; users adjust leading silence manually and preview against bar lines. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) Sayaslicer supports arbitrary snap but explicitly calls proper BPM-change grid/clipboard support a planned feature. [Sayaslicer planned features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features)
- **P0 — Quantization can change the sound.** iBMSC guidance warns that default 192nd snapping can move notes audibly; finer grids can instead create overlap warnings. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/)
- **P1 — Waveform and chart are not one source of truth.** Traditional workflows cut/export in a slicer, then separately paste/drag definitions and notes into BMSE/iBMSC. [BMHelper guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [creation guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)
- **P1 — Reverb tails and silent ends are a manual quality/compliance decision.** Woslicer guide says to choose the final cut for a tail, delete an unwanted silent slice, and keep each asset below one minute; BMS production advice says trim tails but compare backups because over-trimming loses ambience. [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/4de2639ea97bc6723650)

### Interface — P1/P2

- **P1 — Export ceremony is unavoidable.** A typical path is MIDI → BMHelper → DAW render → Woslicer → clipboard import → WAV export → WOS export → BMSE definitions → BMSE sequence paste. [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
- **P1 — Bulk file naming/order is fragile.** BMSE definitions follow Explorer name/drag order and a preselected starting definition; a mismatch silently associates the wrong sound with notes. [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
- **P1 — Debugging is distributed across tools.** A blank filename can disable Woslicer’s total export; unreadable WAVs can crash it; MIDI may need re-saving; locale decimals may need replacement. [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Woslicer wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer) [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) [creation guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)
- **P2 — Discoverability is weak.** Woslicer II relies on many single-key commands; III’s mouse UI is preferred by one user, while Sayaslicer exposes a large shortcut set but retains Woslicer-compatible conventions. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Sayaslicer shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts)

### Settings — P1/P2

- **P1 — Zero-cross is a trade-off, not a free quality switch.** It can reduce clicks but moves markers and may break fine-resolution iBMSC interoperability; the documented workaround is BMSE’s 192nd rounding. [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
- **P1 — “Fade” semantics are easy to misunderstand.** Woslicer III describes fade as attaching a reverse-played version to the end; the intended tail treatment is therefore an export transform, not merely a visual preview. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
- **P1 — Normalize/mastering is outside the slice model.** A BMS author reports that individual key slicing changes bus-compressor behavior and recommends separate master and keysound mixes/stems. [note](https://note.com/qfeileadh/n/n5453cf427b46)
- **P2 — Defaults need per-project and per-slice overrides.** Published Woslicer settings include offset, fade/tail, noise gate (default -48 dB), grid, and BPM; another author changes tail/offset/gate to avoid degradation. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) [note](https://note.com/qfeileadh/n/n5453cf427b46)

### Backend / data model — P0/P1

- **P0 — Destructive export multiplies asset-management cost.** sound-slicer’s documented project requires a source folder and a `wav` subfolder containing the generated samples and BMS; Woslicer/BMSE similarly create many files and definitions. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
- **P0 — Identity is fragile across clipboard and encoding boundaries.** BMS traditionally has 1295 definitions; Base62 extensions raise capacity but not universal compatibility. [creation guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%E9%9F%B3) iBMSC can also write locale-dependent decimal separators. [creation guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)
- **P1 — Format/bit-depth support is a hard failure mode.** Woslicer troubleshooting calls out unreadable WAV and 24/32-bit files; FL Slicer requires WAV for embedded slice markers and cannot use MP3 markers. [Woslicer wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer) [FL manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm)
- **P1 — Deduplication is valuable but not automatic in every workflow.** sound-slicer explicitly contrasts 1000 rhythmic events/1000 slices with melodic reuse of 10; BMHelper/Mid2BMS advertise chord/reuse/quantization assistance. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) [Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/)
- **P1 — Playback semantics depend on the target engine.** Community DJMAX documentation says older single-sample-per-track behavior could cut off the previous sample, while Technika 2 is described as non-interfering; RESPECT V keysounds follow hit timing and can be toggled off. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) [RESPECT guide](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2362889860)

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs. Woslicer — keep these

### Keep from Sayaslicer

1. **One modern cross-platform surface** with drag-and-drop, project save/load, undo/redo, marker copy/paste, and multilingual UI. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
2. **Explicit interoperability modes:** separate BMSE (safe 192nd rounding) and iBMSC (arbitrary resolution) clipboard exports, with an honest warning about zero-cross movement. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
3. **Fast keyboard loop:** marker placement, nearest-snap movement, previous/next marker, preview-and-advance, selection editing, and direct keysound export. [shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts)
4. **Practical cleanup controls:** configurable silent-tail threshold, fadeout, zero-crossing, and partial BPM-change support. [features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
5. **Responsive maintenance:** release notes explicitly address large files, non-stereo waveform/offset preview, drag-and-drop, zoom, resnap-all, and docking/layout. [releases](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases)

### Keep from Woslicer

1. **BPM/offset/grid mental model** that makes a raw waveform map to bars and beats. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
2. **Very low-friction preview:** P previews between cut lines and Enter stops; II’s shortcuts support rapid marker work. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)
3. **Batch export plus portable cut-position metadata (WOS)** so a part can be re-opened or cleared and re-cut. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
4. **BMHelper handoff** for MIDI-derived material, while retaining manual chop mode for automation/non-MIDI audio. [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)

## 4. Top 10 recommendations for DJMax Studio Slicer

1. **P0 — Make the virtual slice the canonical object.** Store `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` plus project-level BPM/offset and per-slice transforms; export WAV/OGG only on finalize. This directly removes the source-of-truth and file-management failure documented in Woslicer/BMSE workflows. [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
2. **P0 — Ship a dual timeline:** waveform/ruler in milliseconds below and Studio chart preview above, linked to one playhead. Existing tools split cutting from chart placement across clipboard/export steps. [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [creation guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)
3. **P0 — Make snap reversible and visible.** Offer 1/4–1/192, arbitrary/ms snap, “marker moved by zero-cross” badges, and a preview of quantization delta. This addresses Sayaslicer’s zero-cross/iBMSC caveat and iBMSC’s audible 192nd-snap warning. [Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) [checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/)
4. **P0 — Add target modes with validators:** BMS, RESPECT, TECHNIKA. Validate sample count, duration, overlap/playback semantics, format, and encoding before export; never silently assume Base36/Base62/engine compatibility. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
5. **P1 — Provide per-slice non-destructive Zero-X / Fade / Normalize overrides.** Show raw boundaries and rendered preview separately, preserve the original range, and support safe reset. The need is evidenced by zero-cross marker movement, tail/fade choices, and mastering differences. [Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) [note](https://note.com/qfeileadh/n/n5453cf427b46)
6. **P1 — Build a Slice Library with deduplication and aliases.** Let users reuse identical virtual ranges or intentionally over-define samples for target engines; show count/capacity and “new vs reused” status. Reuse can turn 500 repeated events into 10 samples, while limits make waste costly. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
7. **P1 — Implement robust undo/redo and draft slices.** A draft boundary should be audition-able before committing a note; support bulk move/resnap and project snapshots. Sayaslicer already demonstrates undo/redo and resnap/navigation value. [shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts) [release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/vb543f80)
8. **P1 — Replace clipboard ceremonies with “Import to Studio” and round-trip export.** Import Woslicer/BMHelper/iBMSC/BMSE data into a project, map identifiers visibly, and export back with a manifest. This eliminates Explorer order, starting-number, locale-decimal, and silent association errors. [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [creation guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)
9. **P1 — Add an automated preflight and repair queue.** Detect unsupported bit depth/codec, missing files, empty filename/output path, >60-second assets, excessive tails, non-stereo edge cases, and incompatible resolution; offer conversion/trim with before/after audition. [Woslicer wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer) [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) [Sayaslicer release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/v74831ea)
10. **P2 — Preserve expert shortcuts but make them discoverable.** Keep P/Enter preview, marker navigation, auto-advance Grid/Beat/Off, and configurable shortcut profiles; add command search/tooltips and a visible shortcut overlay. This retains Woslicer speed without requiring memorization. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) [Sayaslicer shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts)

## Proposed dual-timeline / mode-switcher validation

The proposal is strongly supported by the observed failure boundary: traditional tools produce audio assets first, then separately transfer clipboard sequence/definition data into an editor. [Woslicer workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) Sayaslicer already proves that a single slicer can own waveform markers, snap, preview, undo/redo, project persistence, and both BMS clipboard dialects. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) The missing piece is a shared chart model and target-aware validation, especially because BMS definitions, DJMAX/PTSEQUENCER limits, and playback-interference rules differ by engine. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)

The recommended layout at 1380×860 is: top 55–60% chart preview with notes auto-created from committed slices; bottom 30–35% waveform with ms and beat rulers; a right Slice Library/inspector; and a compact toolbar for Snap, Zero-X, Fade, Normalize, Undo/Redo, Auto-advance, and target mode. Keep raw and rendered preview toggles adjacent, because zero-cross/fade changes can alter the exported sound while the source remains intact. [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
